methods.label: Bound the distance from the center
methods.explanation:
A point is inside or on the circle exactly when its distance from the center is at most \(10\). For \((x,-x)\), the horizontal and vertical differences from \((5,5)\) are \(x-5\) and \(-x-5\). The distance formula therefore gives the equivalent condition
\[
(x-5)^2+(-x-5)^2\le 10^2.
\]
Expanding makes the linear terms cancel:
\[
2x^2+50\le100,
\]
so \(x^2\le25\), or \(-5\le x\le5\).

Every integer in this interval gives a distinct point. Both endpoints satisfy equality in the distance condition, so they are included. The number of integers is
\[
5-(-5)+1=\boxed{11},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses the Pythagorean distance formula, expansion of squares, and an inclusive integer count.
